h1: three ways to find ur moon sign, one of them free
dek: ur rashi is the moon sign, not the sun sign. u can compute it, u can ask ur family, or u can work backwards from the syllable ur name was chosen from. here is all three, with the full nakshatra pada syllable table.

faq.a: the sidereal sign the moon occupied at ur birth. in indian practice this is ur rashi, and it is what families mean when they ask for it. the sun sign is a different and much less used measurement.

faq.q: what do i need to find my moon sign?
faq.a: ur birth date, a rough birth time and ur birth place. the moon crosses a sign in about 2.25 days, so the date usually settles it and the time only matters near a boundary.

faq.q: can i find my moon sign from my name?
faq.a: often, yes. many indian names are chosen from a syllable assigned to the nakshatra pada the moon occupied at birth. if ur formal naming syllable is known, the table works backwards to a nakshatra and from there to a rashi.

the naming ceremony. one traditional method picks the first syllable of the name from the moon's nakshatra pada at birth, which is why so many families have a formal name that differs from the one used at home.

faq.q: why does my app give a different moon sign to my family?
faq.a: almost always an ayanamsa problem. if the app is set to tropical rather than sidereal, positions land about 24 degrees ahead, which moves the sign. check that lahiri is selected.

faq.q: how precise does my birth time need to be?
faq.a: for the sign, a rough time is usually enough. for the nakshatra u want it to the hour, and for the pada or the dasha start date u want it to the minute.

faq.q: what if i was born near a sign boundary?
faq.a: then the hour decides it. the moon covers about half a degree an hour, so a placement in the last or first degree of a sign needs a real birth time rather than an estimate.

faq.q: is the moon sign the same as the nakshatra?
faq.a: no. there are 12 rashis and 27 nakshatras, so each sign contains two and a quarter nakshatras. the nakshatra is the finer measurement and it is what the dasha is calculated from.

faq.q: why does indian astrology use the moon and not the sun?
faq.a: because the moon moves fast, so it distinguishes people born days apart, and because it carries the mind. it also starts the vimshottari dasha and is what kundli matching is scored on.

faq.q: can i find my moon sign without any birth time at all?
faq.a: usually yes for the sign, since the moon spends over two days in each one. u may not be able to settle the nakshatra, and u will not be able to compute an accurate dasha start.
the same thing. janma means birth, so janma rashi is the birth moon sign. u will also see chandra rashi used for it.

faq.q: does the moon sign change over my life?
faq.a: no. it is fixed at birth. the transiting moon changes sign every couple of days, but ur birth moon sign never moves.
